column1: # G7 phases 3-4: provenance -- WHY the value at a path holds
# record as a JSON object: `value` and the ordered `conjuncts`
# (each {canon, role, site}), or `code` and `note` when the answer
# is a refusal. A finding's `message` is excluded, as every other
# verb's goldens exclude it: prose is per-port, codes are not.
# A CONTRIBUTION is a value the author WROTE that met something at
# this path. Values the engine mints on the way (a kind lifted while
# a disjunct trials its members, a fold's intermediate) are not
# contributions; nor are the members INSIDE one written value, which
# meet at the same path as that value resolves. A conjunct is the
# exception in the other direction: its terms are separately written
# and each has its own site, so it expands.
# Roles: literal, spread (a template applied to this key), ref (the
# reference itself, whose canon names its target) and pref.
# Contributions are in SOURCE order -- file, row, column -- not meet
# order, which is the fixpoint's business and a parity risk.
# Every expectation was obtained by the parity probe (AGENTS.md):
# both engines were run over this corpus and diffed field by field
# A WRITTEN CALL NAMES ITS FUNCTION: a compound's site always names its
# opening token, not the whole call -- see the round-trip note in
# patch.tsv. (An UNSITED conjunct row stood here while the pipe
# existed: `x |> upper` synthesised a call the parser never sited.
# ADR-018 removed the pipe, and with it the one spelling that could
# put an unsited conjunct in a document.)
# PROVENANCE THROUGH CLONES (the review's finding E). Every row below
# is a value that reached its path by being CLONED from something the
# author wrote -- a spread template applied per key, a pack()
# generator, an id()-merge -- and the answer must name the line the
# author can edit. The recorder used to decide "did the author write
# this" by looking the operand's id up in a set stamped over the
# parsed tree, which is true of the parsed tree and of nothing derived
# from it, so all three families answered "(no contributions: nothing
# met at this path)" over values `why` had just printed.
# THE SIBLING PAIR IS THE POINT of the first two: identical statements
# under one template, and the record has to read the same for both.
# It did not -- the first key reported the written `*1|integer` as one
# contribution and the second reported `*1` and `integer` as two,
# because the template's own child had been advanced in place between
# the two applications (use-cases/BUGS.md §22). A row per position is
# what the review asked for, so the instability cannot come back
# unnoticed by covering only the first child.

column1: # TOP IS THE UNIT ELEMENT, not something the author wrote, so a path
# holding it has no contribution and says so -- the one shape that
# still answers "nothing met at this path" now that the value which
# STANDS at a path counts (finding E).
# A NESTED JUNCTION carried through a REFERENCE reports the statement
# the author wrote, once: the fold's narrowed form stands at the same
# token, and one written token is one contribution.
# A SPREAD IS A SPREAD FROM EITHER SIDE. Every row above writes the
# template and the keys in ONE statement, which is the own-key path.
# Written as two duplicate statements the template arrives as a PEER,
# and that arm did not mark it -- so the same document reported the
# `spread` role or dropped it (reporting `literal`) depending only on
# how the author spaced their statements (BUGS.md §55). The ListVal
# twin already marked its peer arm, which is what said which side was
